title: Flow Net Seepage Quantity

q.description: Seepage flow per unit length of dam

H.description: Total head (difference between upstream and downstream water levels)

Nf.description: Number of flow channels in the flow net

applicability: For homogeneous, isotropic section. For anisotropic soils, transform section: x_transformed = x × √(kv/kh). For zoned dams, use numerical seepage analysis.

title: Filter Retention Criterion (USBR/USACE)
applicability: Simplified criterion. USBR method adjusts based on percent finer than No. 200 sieve in base soil: if > 85% finer than No. 200, D15F ≤ 9 × d85B (regraded). Full USBR procedure considers base soil gradation category (1–4) and adjusts D15F limit accordingly.

title: Filter Permeability Criterion
applicability: Ensures filter is at least 25× more permeable than base soil (k ∝ D²). For drains, permeability must also handle the design seepage flow: Q = k × i × A.
source: USBR DS-13 Ch5, Terzaghi filter criteria

title: Exit Gradient (Vertical — Foundation Piping)

i_exit.description: Hydraulic gradient at the downstream exit point

Δh.description: Head loss between last two equipotential lines at exit

applicability: Critical gradient i_cr ≈ (Gs-1)(1-n) ≈ 1.0. Factor of safety against piping: FS = i_cr / i_exit. Required FS ≥ 3.0–4.0 (USACE), ≥ 2.0–3.0 (USBR). Weighted filter or drainage blanket at toe reduces exit gradients.

title: Significant Wave Height (SMB Method)
equation: Hs = 0.0016 × √(F) × U²/g (approximate, deep water, fully developed)
alt_form: USACE SPM: Hs = f(U, F, d) from nomographs

F.description: Fetch length (distance of open water over which wind blows)

U.description: Wind speed (adjusted for overwater, duration, elevation)

applicability: Simplified version — use USACE Shore Protection Manual or CEM for detailed analysis. Wind speed adjustments: overwater factor 1.1, duration adjustment for fetch-limited vs duration-limited.
source: USACE Shore Protection Manual (SPM), USBR DS-13 Ch6

title: Wind Setup (Water Surface Tilt)

S.description: Wind setup — rise in water level at downwind shore

applicability: Zuider Zee formula. SI form: S = U²F/(g×d_avg) × 3.5×10⁻⁶. Typically small (0.01–0.30 m) for most reservoirs but can be significant for shallow, long-fetch reservoirs.

title: Riprap Sizing — Hudson Formula (Upstream Slope)

θ.description: Angle of embankment slope from horizontal

applicability: Originally for breakwater armor but adapted for dam slopes. USACE method (ETL 1110-2-334) provides alternative. Minimum riprap layer thickness = 1.5 × D50 or D100, whichever is greater. Must be placed on a properly designed bedding/filter layer.

title: Grout Curtain Depth Guideline

D_grout.description: Depth of grout curtain below dam foundation

applicability: USBR guideline for initial sizing. Deeper at abutments (wrap around flanks). Actual depth determined by geological conditions — grouting continues until Lugeon values < 3–5 Lu are achieved. Multiple rows may be needed in highly fractured rock.

title: Blanket Theory — Required Weight for Exit Gradient Control

FS.description: Factor of safety against heave at downstream blanket edge

γ_b.description: Submerged unit weight of blanket material

h_excess.description: Excess artesian head above ground surface at blanket edge

applicability: For alluvial foundation with natural impervious blanket downstream. FS ≥ 1.5–2.0. If blanket is thin or absent, relief wells or weighted berm required.

title: Freeboard Computation
equation: Freeboard = IDF surcharge + wave runup + wind setup + settlement + safety margin

IDF_surcharge.description: Rise in reservoir level during IDF routing above normal pool

wave_runup.description: Height of wave runup on the dam slope

settlement.description: Long-term crest settlement allowance (1–5% of height)

applicability: Crest elevation = Normal max pool + freeboard. USBR requires minimum 3 ft (0.9 m) freeboard above maximum water surface from PMF routing. USACE similar. For significant/low hazard dams, reduced IDF may be used.
